claims.claim: Circle dates Stellar support to 2026-05-18 and the public-live announcement to 2026-05-19.

sources.quote: The page date is 2026-05-19 and it says Circle CCTP is live on Stellar.
May 19. CCTP is now live on @StellarOrg.

claims.notes: The support record and public announcement remain separate milestones.

claims.claim: Use CctpForwarder with correct mintRecipient or destinationCaller for G/M/C funds.

sources.quote: Use CctpForwarder for G, M, or C recipients; set both fields to it; wrong values can leave funds permanently stuck.
Circle's source includes the on-chain Stellar CctpForwarder.

claims.notes: The current reference explicitly covers all three StrKey recipient types.

claims.claim: The 6-decimal CCTP format leaves Stellar USDC's seventh decimal on Stellar.

sources.quote: CCTP messages use six-decimal subunits; an outbound seventh-decimal amount stays in the user's Stellar account.
The Stellar implementation is the source boundary for seven-local-to-six-canonical normalization.

claims.notes: Circle's example leaves 0.0000007 USDC in the Stellar account.

sources.quote: Retrieve the current route fee from GET /v2/burn/USDC/fees; Standard is free and Fast varies by route.

claims.notes: Production and sandbox still match the 2026-07-11 readings. A fresh query remains required.

claims.claim: Treats Circle fees, network resources, relayers, integrators, and swaps as distinct costs.

sources.quote: This page defines the route-specific CCTP Fast Transfer fee.
Stellar CCTP also uses separate on-chain Soroban and integration components.

claims.notes: Protocol fees do not subsume costs charged by separate networks or providers.

Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://developers.circle.com/cctp/references/stellar — CCTP uses six decimals and leaves seventh-decimal dust on Stellar.
Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://iris-api.circle.com/v2/burn/USDC/fees/27/0 — live 27→0 remains 0/0; the companion 0→27 route remains 1/0.
Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://developers.circle.com/cctp/concepts/fees — Circle defines route fees separately from other integration costs.
